covered: Geography as a spatial, systems science with physical and human parents.
Earth's place in the solar system and the conditions that make the surface habitable.
The Earth's oblate-spheroid shape, size, gravity variation and the geoid.
Eratosthenes' shadow experiment and the logic of measuring the Earth.
Why the UPSC syllabus begins with the Earth's frame, and why maps are arguments.
lastHandoff.next: Lesson 2: The Grid We Live By — latitude, longitude, time zones and the International Date Line. Open by recalling that Eratosthenes measured an arc on a sphere; now we need a coordinate system to describe any point on it.
lastHandoff.notes: The student now has the shape, size and a first model of measurement. Do not repeat the solar-system material. Reuse the Eratosthenes logic when explaining longitude and time: 15° of longitude equals one hour. Make the arithmetic concrete with a Delhi–New York flight and with India's single standard meridian at 82°30′E. Keep the critical map-reading stance from the final section; it will return in the projection lesson.
